description: A pool of neutral filler sentences, the facts buried in them, per-needle near-miss distractors, and two-fact chains for distributed reasoning. The filler is deliberately dull and free of the tokens the needles carry, so a model cannot answer from the haystack alone; the distractors belong to the needle they surround, because a distractor about a different fact distracts from nothing.
filler: The depot inspection team meets on the first working day of each month.
Pallets are wrapped before they leave the marshalling area, without exception.
The night shift hands over to the morning shift in the west office.
Forklift batteries are rotated through the charging bay in a fixed order.
Cold storage is inspected by the same contractor who maintains the loading bay doors.
Deliveries arriving without a manifest are held in the quarantine aisle.
The site's fire drill is announced by a long tone followed by two short ones.
Visitors sign in at the gatehouse and are escorted while on the yard.
Damaged crates are photographed before they are broken down for recycling.
The stock reconciliation report is circulated after the weekly count.
Aisle markings are repainted whenever they become difficult to read.
Radio channels are assigned per team and are not shared between shifts.
The mezzanine is used for slow-moving lines and seasonal overflow.
Empty containers are stacked no more than four high against the north wall.
The maintenance log lives in the workshop and is completed at the end of each task.
Personal protective equipment is issued at the gatehouse and returned on departure.
Trailers are chocked before any loading begins.
The yard is swept at the end of the late shift.
Temperature readings are taken from the same three points every day.
Spill kits are positioned at every corner of the main aisle.
Outbound consignments are checked against the picking sheet twice.
The label printer in the packing area is reserved for outbound work.
Returns are logged before they are inspected, never afterwards.
A supervisor signs off any movement between bonded and general stock.
The staff canteen closes half an hour before the late shift begins.
Bicycles are stored in the rack beside the gatehouse and not on the yard.
Site inductions are repeated for anyone who has been away for a full season.
The compactor is emptied whenever the indicator reaches the marked line.
Hand scanners are docked overnight so that they are charged for the morning.
Pick faces are replenished from the reserve locations directly above them.
The goods-in office keeps a paper copy of every signed delivery note.
Any near miss is reported before the end of the shift in which it happened.
Racking is inspected annually by an external engineer.
The training room doubles as the muster point briefing area.
Shrink wrap is ordered in bulk and stored in the consumables cage.
Broken pallets are separated from serviceable ones at the point of use.
The site plan on the wall of the west office is the authoritative copy.
Contractors work to a permit that names the area and the hours.
Aisle lighting is on a sensor and stays on for a fixed period after movement.
The dock levellers are tested each week and the test is recorded.
